name: Foundry Broadfoot Work Sneaker
description:
A wide-platform sneaker with a removable footbed system designed for augmented workers whose prosthetic feet are larger or differently weighted than standard shoe lasts accommodate. The toe box is unusually deep and wide, the outsole a chunky flat rubber platform. It comes in three widths and the insole stack is user-adjustable with included shims. Looks like an oversized utilitarian sneaker — functional ugliness worn with indifference.

The Foundry Broadfoot is the most common aug-compatible shoe on the Shelf and lower Tier 2. It's cheap, it works, and it doesn't pretend to be anything else.
functionality: Extra-wide, extra-deep toe box for large-format prosthetic feet. User-adjustable insole shim system for height and weight distribution compensation.
what_it_says: You're working class, augmented, and stretching every quanta. No shame in it.
worn_by: prosthetic users with non-standard foot profiles
people who can't afford fitted aug-footwear
story_hooks: The shim system is generic enough that people use Foundry footbeds to modify non-aug shoes — a small trade in modified footbeds exists on the Shelf.
A Foundry Broadfoot in good condition found at a crime scene is notable — it means the owner took care of things, which says something about them.

physical_description.visual_profile: Brutalist utilitarian sneaker with exaggerated proportions—chunky, wide-set silhouette that reads industrial and unapologetically functional. The platform sole dominates the profile, making the wearer appear slightly elevated. Despite its bulk, it has an honest, no-frills aesthetic that signals practical necessity over fashion.
physical_description.fit: Deliberately oversized through the toe box and midfoot to accommodate prosthetic augmentations of varying sizes and weight distributions. Relaxed, almost boxy fit with aggressive arch support. Three width options available for custom accommodation.
physical_description.primary_material: Ballistic nylon upper with reinforced synthetic leather panels at heel and toe strike zones. Chunky rubber outsole in industrial gray-black compound. Removable footbed system with nylon-backed insole.
physical_description.texture: Rough, utilitarian—matte nylon with slightly textured synthetic leather overlays. The outsole has deep lugs with visible molding seams. Insole stack is firm and modular, designed for frequent adjustment.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal gray nylon upper with black synthetic leather reinforcements. Outsole in deep anthracite with worn concrete-gray platform. Minimal branding in faded white stencil.
physical_description.closures: Standard lace system with friction-lock eyelets. No magnetic or tech-assisted fastening—reliability over novelty.
distinctive_features: Removable modular footbed system with included adjustment shims
Exceptionally deep and wide toe box to clear prosthetic feet
Chunky flat platform sole (approximately 1.5 inches) for weight distribution
Reinforced heel and toe strike zones in synthetic leather
Faded 'Foundry Goods Co.' stencil on tongue and heel
Visible stitching and seams—no attempt to hide construction
Three width variants (Standard, Wide, XWide) marked subtly on insole
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2-3 functional. Ubiquitous on the Shelf and lower Tier 2—the working aug's standard-issue footwear.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by augmented laborers, industrial workers, prosthetic users, and anyone whose augmentation requires accommodation over aesthetics. Signals no-nonsense practicality and acceptance of cyborg existence. Zero fashion pretension.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in and scuffed within weeks. Outsole shows worn flat spots at heel and ball of foot. Laces often frayed or replaced with industrial cord. The shoe looks better the more beaten it gets—its utilitarian purpose becomes more evident with wear.
